title: THE KNIGHT WHO WON BY ACCIDENT
text: {{other}} boasts of never losing a duel. You discover the previous opponents were paid to surrender. Unfortunately, the next challenge has just been addressed to you.

choices.label: Ask the champion what surrender pays

outcome.text: {{other}} gives you six gold to preserve the legend. You fall over after a magnificently unconvincing blow and spend the walk home rehearsing a better groan.

choices.label: Invite the previous opponents to demonstrate

outcome.text: Three former victims demonstrate the same fatal stagger. {{other}} objects that you have organised a very unfair rehearsal.

choices.label: Insist on a real practice bout (injury risk)

outcome.text: {{other}} has to lift a sword without paying anyone first. The spectators become attentive for entirely new reasons.

stakes.summary: A real bout can injure either opponent.

title: THE LOVE LETTER THAT ESCAPED
text: Your private love letter has reached the wrong hearth. Three neighbours consider the description flattering. {{spouse}} would like to know which of them resembles a summer orchard.

choices.label: Read the original aloud, including the intended name

outcome.text: {{spouse}} hears the name before the unfortunate fruit comparison. The misunderstanding ends; the orchard will take longer to live down.

choices.label: Claim it was an exercise for a travelling poet

outcome.text: {{spouse}} asks you to recite another verse. Your sudden objection to poetry is much less convincing than the first letter.

choices.label: Dedicate the entire disastrous poem to your spouse

outcome.text: You recite it under your own window. {{spouse}} pulls you inside before the orchard can acquire another harvest.

title: THE NOBLE’S BRILLIANT DISGUISE
text: {{other}} arrives in a sack with a coronet underneath and insists the name is “Ordinary John”. Ordinary John would like to hear an honest opinion of the local nobility.

choices.label: Give Ordinary John an ordinary load to carry

outcome.text: {{other}} carries it three steps before requesting the sort of assistance usually reserved for important people. You praise the remarkable speed of the promotion.

choices.label: Describe exactly what the households complain about

outcome.text: {{other}} forgets to disguise the voice halfway through defending the lord. The argument becomes considerably more useful after that.

choices.label: Remark how handsome the disguised lord must be

outcome.text: {{other}} agrees before remembering not to know. You are both obliged to admire the sack for a moment.

title: THE WEDDING SPEECH THAT WILL NOT END
text: {{other}} asks you to toast a newly married couple. A hiccup arrives after the first name and appears determined to marry it to every sentence.

choices.label: Offer the shortest possible blessing

outcome.text: You say “Happiness”, hiccup once and sit. {{other}} calls it the most efficient speech of the feast.

choices.label: Make the interruption part of a song

outcome.text: The guests join in at the wrong places. {{other}} has to explain to the bride’s aunt that this was not a family custom until five minutes ago.

choices.label: Refuse to surrender the rest of your magnificent speech

outcome.text: The couple finish eating before you finish the introduction. {{other}} moves the candle farther from your sleeve without interrupting the hiccups.

title: THE LADDER AT THE WRONG WINDOW
text: {{other}} waits below a dark window with flowers. You know the room belongs to an elderly wool sorter who has already opened a bucket.

choices.label: Move the admirer before the bucket tips

outcome.text: {{other}} escapes with dry flowers and a much wetter opinion of the address supplied by a friend.

choices.label: Announce the serenade to its actual audience

outcome.text: The wool sorter demands a second verse. {{other}} receives the bucket only after failing to supply one.

choices.label: Take the first verse yourself

outcome.text: The bucket finds you instead. {{other}} helps wring out your cloak and promises never to praise your voice again.

title: THE SLEEVES THAT ARRIVED BEFORE YOU
text: {{other}} lends you fashionable sleeves for an important supper. They reach the soup before your hands and the candle before your judgement.

choices.label: Roll them up and admit the loan

outcome.text: You eat with both hands visible. {{other}} asks why nobody told the tailor this was an available arrangement.

choices.label: Continue the magnificent gestures

outcome.text: The left sleeve extinguishes a candle and the right acquires somebody else’s sauce. {{other}} retrieves the sleeves before they can accept a third invitation.

choices.label: Ask your neighbour to hold the spare fabric

outcome.text: The two of you conduct supper like an awkward sail. {{other}} is delighted until asked to steer the pudding.

title: THE HERO WITH A RHYME MISSING
text: {{other}} commissions a song about your courage. The minstrel has found rhymes for your name, but all of them involve a cowardly act or a skin complaint.

choices.label: Become the hero under a less musical name

outcome.text: The song praises a stranger with your deeds. {{other}} enjoys it until the stranger is credited with paying for supper.

choices.label: Suggest the embarrassing incident yourself

outcome.text: The audience laughs where you intended. {{other}} has to surrender the much worse version prepared for later.

choices.label: Demand that courage rhyme with your name

outcome.text: The minstrel stretches the word across three notes. {{other}} starts coughing at every repetition and finally leaves the room to recover.

title: THE CHAMPION’S VERY SMALL WEAPON
text: {{other}} challenges you to spit a cherry stone farther than the village champion. The champion is the baker’s grandmother and has removed her good shoes.

choices.label: Compete with suitable respect

success.text: Your stone passes hers. {{other}} congratulates you at a careful distance from the grandmother’s second attempt.

failure.text: Your stone lands in your own collar. {{other}} declares this an entirely different achievement.

choices.label: Judge the distances instead

outcome.text: {{other}} disputes half a thumb’s length until the grandmother offers to demonstrate it against a nearby target. The dispute ends.

choices.label: Kick your stone farther while everyone watches hers

outcome.text: The grandmother has been watching your feet. {{other}} awards you a special prize for having apparently misunderstood the sport.

title: THE DANCE WITH ONE INSTRUCTION TOO MANY
text: {{other}} teaches a fashionable dance before the lord’s supper. Every step has a name. Your feet know none of them.

choices.label: Offer a simpler village measure

outcome.text: The servants recognise the tune and the nobles borrow their timing. {{other}} calls this the rustic portion of an increasingly successful evening.

choices.label: Invent names for the mistakes

outcome.text: The audience follows the second mistake willingly. {{other}} is obliged to explain why the dance now contains “Avoid the Chair”.

choices.label: Stop before taking anyone else with you

outcome.text: You leave the floor with a bow that requires no assistance. {{other}} praises your judgement in the voice usually used for the injured.

title: THE MERCHANT’S FABULOUSLY EMPTY FEAST
text: {{other}} invites the important buyers to admire a new fortune. The dishes are magnificent, the portions are tiny and the cook has begun serving the decorations.

choices.label: Turn it into a shared supper

outcome.text: You bring bread and invite everyone to add what they have. {{other}} acquires a warm evening at the cost of a rather cold pretence.

choices.label: Praise the remarkable lightness of every course

outcome.text: The buyers repeat the compliment until {{other}} orders the cook to make something heavy. The cook brings the pot.

choices.label: Leave hungry without exposing the host

outcome.text: {{other}} follows you to the door with an apology wrapped round the last piece of cheese.

title: THE HAT THAT FRIGHTENS ITS OWNER
text: {{other}} acquires a plumed hat to make an impression at court. A gust makes the plume brush the back of the neck. The resulting leap makes a different impression.

choices.label: Catch the hat before the second attack

outcome.text: {{other}} thanks you and holds the hat at arm’s length for the rest of the introduction.

choices.label: Bow solemnly to the victorious feather

outcome.text: The servants copy the bow. {{other}} removes the plume with the expression of someone dismissing a dangerous officer.

choices.label: Offer to tame the creature yourself

outcome.text: You wear the hat backwards. {{other}} is forced to choose between gratitude and explaining why this looks better.

title: THE HERMIT WHO ENJOYS VISITORS
text: {{other}} invites you to meet a famous hermit. The hermit offers three courses, asks who else is coming and complains that solitude has been slow this season.

choices.label: Let the lonely host talk

outcome.text: The hermit tells you about the winter. {{other}} quietly stops explaining the advantages of never needing anybody.

choices.label: Invite the hermit to your next supper

outcome.text: The invitation is accepted before you have named a date. {{other}} wonders whether a hermit may bring a companion.

choices.label: Ask whether the wilderness requires a waiting room

outcome.text: The hermit finds an excellent view for you outside. {{other}} remains for the second course.

title: THE NOBLE’S PROOF OF COURAGE
text: {{other}} offers to demonstrate courage by approaching an allegedly savage pig. The pig is asleep. Its owner recommends leaving both facts undisturbed.

choices.label: Declare the beast subdued before waking it

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts the triumph in a whisper. The pig sleeps through its own defeat.

choices.label: Wake the pig and let courage take its course

outcome.text: The pig rises, sniffs and follows the smell of the feast. {{other}} retreats faster than anyone expected a victory to travel.

choices.label: Show how its owner actually handles it

outcome.text: You lead it away with food. {{other}} asks whether anyone needs to mention the food in the account of your bravery.

title: THE RIVAL WHO ARRIVED SIDEWAYS
text: {{other}} rides into the square rehearsing a splendid greeting. The saddle begins to turn halfway through it.

choices.label: Hold the reins before the speech falls off

outcome.text: {{other}} completes the greeting from the ground. Thanks follows considerably later, but it does follow.

choices.label: Ask the crowd to admire the new riding style

outcome.text: {{other}} spends the evening explaining how little the incident mattered. By nightfall, even the stable boy knows which side landed first.

choices.label: Offer a private lesson in checking the girth

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts after making it clear that the lesson concerns the saddle’s conduct.

title: THE PERSON YOUR SPOUSE KEEPS PRAISING
text: {{spouse}} has praised a stranger’s looks three times. You discover the portrait being admired is a very flattering picture of you.

choices.label: Admit the resemblance before demanding an apology

outcome.text: {{spouse}} studies you, then the picture, then asks whether the painter can also improve your hearing.

choices.label: Agree that the stranger seems delightful

outcome.text: You compliment the painted face until {{spouse}} turns it round. Supper includes a surprisingly detailed discussion of modesty.

choices.label: Insist this proves something suspicious anyway

outcome.text: {{spouse}} puts the portrait away. The room becomes less handsome and much less willing to explain itself.

title: THE PROPOSAL THAT STUCK
text: You plan a graceful greeting for {{other}} and take one last bite of pear. The greeting arrives as an urgent request for help with the pear.

choices.label: Start again after you can speak

outcome.text: {{other}} hears the real greeting between two small laughs. The second attempt has fewer ornaments and a better answer.

choices.label: Pretend the coughing was an elaborate bow

outcome.text: {{other}} returns the bow while trying not to laugh. You have introduced an unfortunate new custom between you.

choices.label: Retreat with what remains of your dignity

outcome.text: {{other}} offers water for the retreat. Your dignity has to accept it before leaving.

title: THE ROMANCE WITH VERY CLEAR FOOTPRINTS
text: {{spouse}} points to two sets of muddy footprints outside a neighbour’s window. Yours lead there and back. You were returning a borrowed kettle; the kettle has not stayed to testify.

choices.label: Fetch the kettle and its owner

outcome.text: The owner arrives carrying the kettle and an excellent memory for the handle you broke. {{spouse}} forgives the supposed romance before discussing the handle.

choices.label: Explain that many people own feet

outcome.text: {{spouse}} agrees, then asks how many of them wear your patched left shoe. The argument acquires a very specific shape.

choices.label: Admit the broken handle before anything else

outcome.text: {{spouse}} asks why a kettle was worth such an impressive effort to appear unfaithful. The two of you finish laughing before supper.

title: THE BABY WHO CHOSE THE IMPORTANT GUEST
text: {{other}} brings a visiting dignitary to admire a new baby. The baby reaches for the grand chain and immediately decides it is worth tasting.

choices.label: Offer a wooden toy in exchange

outcome.text: The baby releases the chain. {{other}} watches the dignitary thank a piece of wood for succeeding where rank had failed.

choices.label: Congratulate the baby on excellent judgement

outcome.text: {{other}} has to hold the baby while the guest removes the chain. Neither appears willing to be the first to apologise.

choices.label: Take the baby and the responsibility

outcome.text: The baby releases the chain and grips your sleeve. {{other}} calls this a happy transfer of government.

title: THE HERO HIDING BEHIND THE RIGHT DOOR
text: {{other}} hides from a noisy quarrel behind a cellar door. Opening it lets out the household’s enormous dog, which ends the quarrel immediately. Witnesses are cheering the courage.

choices.label: Praise the dog’s contribution

outcome.text: The owner feeds the actual hero. {{other}} accepts a smaller share of the applause without having to re-enter the cellar.

choices.label: Help improve the story

outcome.text: {{other}} becomes increasingly brave with each telling and increasingly dependent on your silence.

choices.label: Get the frightened neighbour away from the crowd

outcome.text: {{other}} stops shaking once the cheering is two streets away. You let the dog have the rest of the story.

title: THE BED MADE FOR A MUCH BETTER PERSON
text: {{other}} has raised a bed to show the household’s importance. Getting into it now requires a servant, a stool and a willingness to be seen needing both.

choices.label: Build a small step and name nobody in particular

outcome.text: {{other}} tests the step after everyone has been asked to leave. The furniture finally becomes suitable for sleeping.

choices.label: Admire the view from the floor

outcome.text: {{other}} descends to explain that height is not the point. This takes both the stool and most of the explanation.

choices.label: Suggest returning the legs to ordinary length

outcome.text: The carpenter lowers the bed while {{other}} is away. You are thanked for the comfort and blamed for the lost elevation.

title: THE FAMILY FEUD LEARNS A TUNE
text: {{other}} whistles a tune associated with an old family insult. Half the lane recognises the insult; the other half keeps asking for the next verse.

choices.label: Supply an embarrassingly affectionate new verse

outcome.text: The tune survives as a love song nobody wants to claim. {{other}} finds it much harder to whistle threateningly.

choices.label: Sing the insulting verse back (family feud)

outcome.text: The lane learns both versions. Your households now possess a quarrel that can be performed without either of you being present.

familyFeud.reason: Public exchange of a family insult

choices.label: Ask what the quarrel is actually about

outcome.text: {{other}} begins with a grandfather, loses track of a cousin and finally admits to never having met either. You agree to leave them out of supper.

title: THE COMPLIMENT YOUR RIVAL BELIEVED
text: {{other}} mistakes your sarcastic praise for a sincere recommendation. The resulting bow is so grateful that the audience has stopped laughing.

choices.label: Let the compliment become true

outcome.text: You help finish the task you had intended to mock. {{other}} thanks you a second time. Resenting the first was much easier.

choices.label: Explain the joke at full volume

outcome.text: The crowd understands. {{other}} understands more than you meant to teach.

choices.label: Suggest a more modest first attempt

outcome.text: {{other}} tries it and succeeds. You are left in the awkward position of having given useful advice.

title: THE SUITOR WHO BROUGHT A PROPMAN
text: {{other}} rehearses a flattering speech to you. A friend behind the hedge supplies the forgotten words and, on one occasion, the wrong beloved’s name.

choices.label: Ask the hedge whether it wishes to join the conversation

outcome.text: The prompter crawls out. {{other}} delivers the remaining sentence without help, and it is much better for being short.

choices.label: Teach the suitor to ask a real question

outcome.text: {{other}} asks what you would actually enjoy doing. The hedge, having no prepared answer, is finally quiet.

choices.label: Leave before the hedge proposes marriage

outcome.text: {{other}} bows alone. The prompter supplies an ending to somebody who is already walking home.

title: THE TRIUMPH THAT REACHED THE WRONG HOUSE
text: {{other}} returns from a modest errand beneath a garland and two borrowed banners. The procession stops at your house because nobody thought to ask where the hero lived.

choices.label: Offer the hero a seat and water

outcome.text: {{other}} sits among the abandoned banners and admits the errand concerned a missing shoe. You ask whether it has returned in triumph too.

choices.label: Lead the procession to the actual destination

outcome.text: The neighbours cheer when the right door finally opens. {{other}} has to acknowledge your contribution to the navigation.

choices.label: Accept the applause yourself

outcome.text: You bow until somebody asks what you did. {{other}} supplies the answer with the joy of someone finally useful to the ceremony.

title: THE WAKE THAT STARTED TOO EARLY
text: {{parent}} falls asleep during preparations for an elderly neighbour’s wake. A visiting mourner begins praising the wrong person’s virtues. {{parent}} opens one eye at the first exaggeration.

choices.label: Make the introduction before the speech improves

outcome.text: The mourner is relieved to discover a living critic. {{parent}} asks to keep the part about generosity for another occasion.

choices.label: Let your parent hear the affectionate part

outcome.text: {{parent}} waits until the kind words are finished before asking for tea. The mourner laughs and stays to share it.

choices.label: Correct the praise as well as the identity

outcome.text: {{parent}} sits up to defend virtues nobody had questioned until you arrived. The actual wake proceeds with rather less help from you.
